**Method 5:** Understand that the Fire element indicates the present, the Air element indicates the future, the Water element indicates the past, and the Earth element indicates sudden or unexpected timing. <note>In geomancy, the four elements are assigned to the four points of a geomantic figure (Shakala) to determine the temporal nature of the question.</note>

If the figure related to the question is situated in its proper place according to the <term>B. J. D. H.</term> <note>An acronym for the four primary houses or elemental arrangements in Arabic geomancy: Beyt (House), Jid (Grandfather), Dahal (Entrance), and Haraj (Exit).</note> sequence, then one should consider its past and future. Based on the tables provided hereafter, one should calculate the time in <term>Ghatikas</term> <note>A traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes.</note>, days, months, and years. If that figure is repeated and is of the <term>Nirgam</term> <note>original: "Kharij" (Outgoing) or "Munkaloub" (Inverted/Mutable)</note> type, the number should be reduced. If it is of the <term>Agam</term> <note>original: "Dakhil" (Incoming) or "Sabit" (Stable/Fixed)</note> type, then adding the count of the repeated figures will determine the exact duration of time. Even if those figures are repeated many times, the calculation should be performed as previously described. If the question figure is not in its proper place within the B. J. D. H. rows, then look at the B. J. D. H. table vertically and horizontally to decide the time and state the number corresponding to that position. If that figure repeats in the <term>Umhat</term> <note>The "Mothers" or the first four houses of a geomantic chart.</note>, consider it as days; if it repeats in the <term>Binhat</term> <note>The "Daughters" or houses 5 through 8.</note>, consider it as weeks; if it repeats in the <term>Mutavalidat</term> <note>The "Resultants" or houses 9 through 12.</note>, consider it as months; and if it repeats in the <term>Jayadat</term> <note>The "Appendices" or final houses/witnesses.</note>, those numbers should be understood as years.

**Method 2:** Multiply the figure in the 1st house by the figure in the house related to the question. Locate the resulting figure within the chart; based on its position and the nature of that figure, consult the table to provide the numerical answer.

**Method 3:** The combination of the 1st house or whichever houses are related to the question is explained hereafter. The answer must be given using all tools such as <term>Takrar</term> <note>Repetition of a figure in different houses.</note>. If those figures repeat in the Umhat, it signifies Ghatikas or days; if they repeat in the Binhat, it signifies days or weeks; if they repeat in the Mutavalidat, it signifies weeks or months; and if they repeat in the Jayadat, it signifies months or years.

**Other Opinions:** If the repeating figure is <term>Sabit</term> (Stable), consider it a year; if it is <term>Dakhil</term> (Incoming), a month; if it is <term>Kharij</term> (Outgoing), a week; and if it is <term>Munkaloub</term> (Inverted), consider it a day.

### ->Determining the Day of the Week.<-

If the figure in the question's house in the chart belongs to the <term>Mizaj</term> <note>Temperament or elemental nature.</note> row corresponding to its original house, then the task will be accomplished on the day of the planet associated with that figure.

### Table for Determining Time According to the B. J. D. H. Sequence
<note>B. J. D. H. refers to the Abjad numerical system used in divination to assign values to figures</note>

The number found there determines the time. Consider that number as the duration of time. Determine the quantity in this manner. See the table on the following pages.

## Table Showing Time Durations According to the Sequence of Letters.

The figures resulting from the multiplication according to the Bi. Ja. Da. Ha. <note>A mnemonic system for geomantic calculations</note> sequence are shown below across 16 figures. At the top of each table, the position-indicating number is placed, followed by the figures of the letter-rows. In the first column of each table below, the position numbers are given, and beneath them are columns for Days, Months, and Years with their respective numbers. The duration should be determined from these. If the resulting figure appears in multiple positions <note>literally "complaining" or "conflicting"</note> frequently, one must establish which is the strongest and determine the days, months, etc., based on that. If determining the strongest figure seems doubtful, one should combine the days, months, and years of all the conflicting positions and divide that total by the number of conflicting positions to determine the time period. This method is utilized in the country of Egypt.

If the desired <term>shakal</term><note>A geomantic figure or sign</note> belongs to the elements of Water or Earth, one should subtract those two numbers. ### Collection of Questions

<note>original: "पूर्वोक्त प्रश्नस्य विधिं वक्ष्ये शिष्य हिताय च ।। लोकानां रंजनार्थं च लिख्यतेऽपि चमत्कृतं ।। २२ ।। तत्प्रश्नस्य विधिं वक्ष्ये साधकानां सुखायं च ।। सर्वेषां प्रश्नजालानां प्रकारं च बहुविधं ।। २३ ।।"</note>
I shall now explain the method of questioning for the benefit of the disciple, written in a wondrous way for the delight of the people. I describe the procedure of these inquiries for the ease of the practitioners, covering the many varieties of all types of questions.

**Meaning:** All the tools required for providing answers to questions were described in Part 1. In this part, the collection of questions necessary for the readers to understand easily has been written with various examples.

### Providing Answers from the 1st House

<note>original: "तनोश्चावयवस्यापि सुखस्याप्यऽसुखस्य च ।। जीवनस्यायुषश्चापि जन्मस्थानभवंतथा ।। २४ ।। बलस्यकार्यारंभस्य प्रयत्नस्य सुखस्य च ।। नृपनीतेश्च शांतेश्च ज्ञेयानि प्रथमगृहात् ।। २५ ।।"</note>
From the first house, one should understand matters regarding the body and its limbs, happiness and sorrow, life and longevity, as well as the place of birth. One should also discern strength, the beginning of tasks, effort, comfort, royal policy <note>political standing or ethics</note>, and peace.

**What are my physical characteristics?** — If the first house contains the <term>Shakal</term> <note>Ramal figure: 2, 2, 1, 2 dots; known as Albus</note>, then there are scars on the head caused by blood disorders like boils; however, these are not painful. 

If it is <note>Ramal figure: 1, 2, 2, 1 dots; known as Laetitia</note>, there is a scar on the left hand caused by a fall from a high place or some other blow. 

If it is <note>Ramal figure: 2, 2, 2, 1 dots; known as Puella</note>, there is a scar on the chest caused by a weapon or a bite from a cruel animal. 

If it is <note>Ramal figure: 1, 2, 2, 2 dots; known as Caput Draconis</note>, there are scars on the back caused by cold-phlegm related diseases or from eating aquatic creatures. 

If it is <note>Ramal figure: 2, 1, 2, 2 dots; known as Puer</note>, there is an injury to the right thigh sustained during a fight. 

If it is <note>Ramal figure: 2, 2, 1, 1 dots; known as Fortuna Minor</note>, there is a wound on the left shoulder caused by a sharp weapon. 

If it is <note>Ramal figure: 1, 1, 1, 2 dots; known as Cauda Draconis</note>, there is a wound in the side caused by a spear or an arrow. 

If it is <note>Ramal figure: 2, 1, 1, 1 dots; known as Fortuna Major</note>, there is a wound on the left thigh caused by a weapon like a pair of tongs or pincers. 

With the remaining figures, there are no ulcers or wounds on the body. Additional characteristics should be understood from the qualities and forms of all sixteen figures described in Part 1.

### Method 2:
If an <term>Entering</term> <note>original: "Dakhil" — a figure moving inward</note> figure is present in the 12th house, the body was robust in the past, but is not so now. If an Entering figure is in the 2nd house, the body will become robust in the future. If it is in the 1st house, it is robust at present. If <term>Unlucky Outgoing</term> <note>original: "Ashubh Kharij" — unfavorable figures moving outward</note> figures are in the above houses, the person is perpetually weak; if <term>Stable Mutable</term> <note>original: "Sabit Munvalib"</note> figures are present, consider the body to be of average build.

### Which is my Planet? —
Count only the total number of points (lines) in all 16 houses and divide that sum by 7. If the remainder is 1, it is Saturn; if 2 remains, Jupiter; 3, Mars; 4, the Sun; 5, Venus; 6, Mercury; and if 7 remains <note>meaning a remainder of 0</note>, consider it to be the Moon.

### Will I live a full life? —
If any of these figures 𝍱 𝍺 𝍩 𝍻 𝍫 𝍲 𝍴 𝍽 appear in the 1st house, one will have a long life (<term>Purnayushi</term>); if 𝍬 𝍯 𝍳 𝍮 appear, a medium lifespan (<term>Madhyamayushi</term>); and if 𝍭 𝍾 𝍿 𝍰 appear, consider it a short lifespan (<term>Alpayushi</term>).

### Method 2:
If the figure in the 4th house "complains" <note>repeats or relates</note> in any of the houses 1, 4, 7, 10, or 13, it indicates a long life. If it complains in houses 2, 5, 8, 11, or 14, a medium lifespan. If it complains in houses 3, 6, 9, 12, or 15, a short lifespan. If it does not complain anywhere, judge based on the figure in the 4th house using the life-expectancy table provided in the first section.

### Method 3:
If the figure in the 4th house complains within the <term>Mothers</term> <note>original: "Umhat" — the first four houses</note>, it indicates a long life. If it complains in the <term>Daughters</term> <note>original: "Binhat" — houses 5-8</note> or the <term>Resultants</term> <note>original: "Mutavallidat" — houses 9-12</note>, a medium lifespan. If it complains in the <term>Witnesses/Judge</term> <note>original: "Javathada" — houses 13-15</note>, consider it a short lifespan.

### Method 4:
Multiply the figures in the 1st and 4th houses. If the resulting figure is <term>Auspicious Entering</term>, it indicates a long life; if <term>Auspicious Stable</term>, a medium life; if <term>Auspicious Mutable</term>, a short life; and if <term>Inauspicious Outgoing</term>, consider the life to be devoid of longevity.

### Will my life pass in happiness? —
If an auspicious figure is in the 1st house, one will be happy; if inauspicious, one will be unhappy and prone to anxiety. If one of 𝍱 𝍺 𝍻 𝍲 𝍳 𝍴 is in that house and complains in the 10th or 5th house...

**Will I obtain wealth?** — If the figure <term>Shakal; a geomantic sign formed by four rows of dots or lines</term> resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 2nd and 4th houses indicates a favorable outcome, then it will be obtained. If any particular <term>Shakal</term><note>A geomantic figure or "sign" used in divination.</note> is present in a house of the <term>Kundali</term><note>The square or circular chart used to map the sixteen geomantic figures.</note>, it will cast a favorable influence on the 3rd, 9th, 5th, 7th, and 11th houses from that position, whether counted clockwise or counter-clockwise, provided favorable figures are situated there.

### Considerations for Buying and Selling:
The 1st house represents the act of selling, and its corresponding house of profit is the 2nd. The 7th house represents the act of buying, and its corresponding house of profit is the 8th. One should provide an answer after observing the auspicious or inauspicious figures in these houses. Alternatively, one may multiply the figures present in those houses and determine the answer based on the auspicious or inauspicious qualities of the resulting figure.

### What if a Purchase is Made?
If an auspicious figure is present in the 2nd, 11th, or 14th houses, there will be profit. If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 7th and 11th houses is one of <sup>I</sup>/<sub>O</sub>, <sup>II</sup>/<sub>O</sub>, or <sup>I</sup>/<sub>OO</sub> <note>These represent specific geomantic binary patterns</note>, and it forms a <term>Takrar</term><note>A "complaint" or connection between houses in geomancy</note> with the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses (the Angles) or the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses (the Succedents), then profit will occur. If the resulting figure is <sup>III</sup>/<sub>O</sub> and it forms a connection with the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses (the Cadents), there will be no profit.

### Method 2:
If there are auspicious figures in the 2nd and 5th houses, or if the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in those houses is one of <sup>I</sup>/<sub>O</sub>, <sup>II</sup>/<sub>I</sub>, <sup>II</sup>/<sub>OO</sub>, or <sup>I</sup>/<sub>OOO</sub>, there will be profit. All other figures should be understood as indicating a loss.

### Method 3:
If one of the figures <sup>II</sup>/<sub>O</sub>, <sup>II</sup>/<sub>I</sub>, or <sup>II</sup>/<sub>OO</sub> is in the 2nd house, and one of <sup>O</sup>/<sub>III</sub> or <sup>I</sup>/<sub>OO</sub> is in the 8th house, then buying will be profitable. If the figures are the opposite of these, then selling will be profitable.

### Will there be Profit in the Metal Trade?
If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 2nd and 10th houses is one of <sup>I</sup>/<sub>O</sub>, <sup>II</sup>/<sub>O</sub>, or <sup>II</sup>/<sub>OO</sub>, then buying is profitable. If the figure <sup>III</sup>/<sub>O</sub> appears, it indicates a loss. If the figure is <sup>O</sup>/<sub>III</sub> or <sup>I</sup>/<sub>OO</sub>, then selling is profitable. If it is <sup>O</sup>/<sub>IO</sub> or <sup>O</sup>/<sub>OOI</sub>, there is a loss in selling. With the figure <sup>II</sup>/<sub>O</sub>, profit comes with delay. If the figure <sup>III</sup>/<sub>O</sub> appears, one should sell quickly. If <sup>O</sup>/<sub>O</sub> or <sup>O</sup>/<sub>OOO</sub> appears, one should buy quickly and not sell. If it is <sup>O</sup>/<sub>O</sub> or <sup>I</sup>/<sub>OO</sub>, it indicates loss. This method applies to everything from base ores <note>original: "dead stone etc."</note> to gold.

### Method 2:
If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 2nd, 10th, and 11th houses is one of <sup>I</sup>/<sub>OIO</sub>, <sup>II</sup>/<sub>OO</sub>, or <sup>I</sup>/<sub>OOO</sub>, then profit will be gained by selling copper.

-> Brothers, sisters, siblings, dreams, and the world; traveling nearby, as well as the nursemaid and the bed. ||28|| Divine tremors, held desires, and the practice of one's own religion; temples and such, always belong to the third house. ||29|| <-

**Do I have brothers and sisters?** — If the figure <term>꠰<br/>꠰<br/>꠰꠰<br/>꠰꠰</term> is in the 3rd house and makes a <term>Takrar</term> <note>original: "takrar"; a technical term in Ramala Shastra referring to the repetition or movement of a figure to another house</note> in an auspicious house or an "entering" house, then they exist.

**How many are there?** — If the figure in the 3rd house is of masculine gender, then there are as many brothers as the number of houses in which it makes a *Takrar*. If it is of feminine gender, know that there are as many sisters as the number of houses in which it makes a *Takrar*.

**Method 2:** Count the number of manifested elements in the <term>Kundali</term> <note>horoscope or geomantic chart</note> separately and set them aside. If the number of manifested points of the Fire and Air elements is greater, then "Brothers" are more numerous. If the number of points of the Water and Earth elements is greater, know that "Sisters" are more numerous.

**Are the brothers and sisters alive?** — If the points of the Fire and Air elements are manifest in the 3rd and 5th houses, they are alive. If the Earth element points are manifest, they have passed away. Alternatively, if the Fire and Air element points are manifest in the 9th house, they are alive; if the Earth element points are manifest, they have passed away.

### How will my end-time be? 
— If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 1st, 4th, 6th, and 8th houses is an **Auspicious Outgoing** <note>Kharij: a figure moving outward</note> figure, then the time of death is near, but one will die without suffering. If it is an **Inauspicious Outgoing** figure, one will die from a fall from a high place. If it is an **Auspicious Incoming** <note>Dakhil: a figure moving inward</note> figure, one will die without any pain. If it is an **Inauspicious Incoming** figure, one will die in pain. If it is an **Auspicious Mobile** <note>Munaqlib: a moving or transformative figure</note> figure, one will die of disease. If it is an **Inauspicious Mobile** figure, one will die with great difficulty. If it is an **Auspicious Stable** <note>Sabit: a fixed or stationary figure</note> figure, one will die of consumption <note>likely tuberculosis</note>, and if it is an **Inauspicious Stable** figure, know that there will be great agony at the moment of death.

### Is there buried wealth? 
— If there is an **Incoming or Stable** figure in the 4th house, it exists. If there is an **Outgoing or Mobile** figure, then it does not.

### Will I obtain land-wealth? 
— If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 4th, 10th, and 2nd houses is an **Auspicious Incoming** figure, it will be obtained soon. If it is **Stable, Outgoing,** or **Mobile**, it will not be obtained.

### Is there land-wealth at this location? 
— If there is an **Incoming or Stable** figure in the 4th house, it is there. If there is an **Outgoing or Mobile** figure, it is not.

**Method 2:** If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 4th and 6th houses is **Incoming or Stable**, it is there. If it is **Mobile**, there is a little, and if it is **Outgoing**, know that there is none.

**Method 3:** If the figures in the 4th and 6th houses are **Incoming or Stable** and auspicious, there is plenty of wealth. If they are inauspicious, there is less.

How deep is it? — The element of Fire <note>Tejas-tattva</note> resides in the upper portion of the 16 figures in the <term>horoscope</term><note>original: "kundali"; here referring to the geomantic chart</note>. ### Predicting Questions from the 5th House.

> <note>original: "पुत्राणां च मुदोद्भूत..."</note> From the house of children (the 5th house), one should predict matters concerning the joy derived from sons, the arrival of a messenger, affection, letters of well-being, and the stability of things given. || 32 || One should also speak of auspicious events, happiness, cleanliness, and curiosity; the good or bad fortune regarding pregnancy, gains, and friends. || 33 || Whether the intellect will be auspicious or inauspicious, matters regarding paternal wealth, and questions about intoxicating substances should all be answered from the 5th house. || 34 ||

**Will she attain her menses (puberty/fertility)?** — Count only the points (lines) in the 15th house of the horoscope and divide that number by 2. If the remainder is 1, she will attain it soon. If the remainder is 0, it will be delayed or will happen through the use of medicine.

**On what kind of garment will the menses first appear?** — If the <term>shakal</term> <note>geomantic figure</note> in the 5th house is <term>[०|०|॥|॥]</term> <note>Albus</note> or <term>[I|I|०|०]</term> <note>Puella</note>, it will occur naturally on excellent clothing; the result of this is auspicious. If it is <term>[०|I|०|I]</term> <note>Populus</note>, it will occur on expensive clothing that has been washed once or twice; the result is good. If it is <term>[०|०|०|I]</term>, <term>[०|०|I|०]</term>, <term>[०|I|I|०]</term>, <term>[I|I|I|I]</term>, <term>[०|०|०|०]</term>, <term>[I|०|०|०]</term>, <term>[०|०|I|०]</term>, or <term>[०|I|०|०]</term>, it will occur on very old and poor quality clothes; the result of this is bad. If it is <term>[I|I|I|I]</term> <note>Via</note>, <term>[I|०|I|I]</term>, <term>[I|I|०|०]</term>, or <term>[०|०|०|०]</term>, it will be on good multi-colored clothes, and the result is also good. And if it is <term>[०|I|०|०]</term> or <term>[०|I|०|०]</term>, it will be on new multi-colored clothes, and the result is also good.

**Will I have children?** — If the <term>shakal</term> in the 5th house is <term>[०|०|॥|॥]</term>, <term>[I|I|०|०]</term>, <term>[I|I|I|I]</term>, <term>[०|०|I|I]</term>, <term>[I|I|०|०]</term>, <term>[०|I|०|I]</term>, <term>[I|०|I|०]</term>, or <term>[I|०|०|I]</term>, then children will be born. The remaining figures are doubtful.

**Method 2:** — If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in the 1st, 5th, 6th, and 7th houses is an "entering" (stable) figure, then children will be born. If the resulting figure is <term>[०|०|I|I]</term>, <term>[I|I|०|०]</term>, or <term>[०|०|०|०]</term>, they will be born after some time. If the figure is <term>[०|०|I|I]</term> or <term>[०|०|I|I]</term>, a miscarriage will occur. With the remaining figures, children will not be born.

**Method 3:** — If there are "entering" (<term>dakhil</term>) or "moving" (<term>munaklib</term>) figures in the 5th, 9th, 11th, 14th, or 15th houses, children will be born.

# Inquiry into Disease

The 1st house represents the patient; the 4th house represents the medicinal remedies. Some <term>Ramal-knowers</term><note>Practitioners of geomancy</note> use the 2nd and 10th houses for medicinal remedies. The 6th house represents the disease; the 10th house represents the physician; the 11th house represents the recovery of the patient; and the 12th house represents the worsening of the disease. If auspicious figures are in the above houses, consider it a good omen; if inauspicious, consider it a bad omen.

# Will the Disease be Cured or Not?

If in the 6th house there is a <term>Kharij</term><note>Outgoing/Mobile figure</note> or <term>Munkalib</term><note>Changeable/Movable figure</note> that is auspicious, the patient will recover quickly. If it is inauspicious, recovery will be delayed and difficult to achieve. If <term>Dakhol</term><note>Incoming/Stable figure</note> or <term>Sabit</term><note>Fixed/Stationary figure</note> figures are present—whether auspicious or inauspicious—the patient will not recover.

**Method 2:** If <term>Kharij</term> or <term>Munkalib</term> figures are in houses 1 to 8, whether auspicious or inauspicious, the patient will recover soon. If <term>Dakhol</term> or <term>Sabit</term> figures are present, whether auspicious or inauspicious, they will not recover.

**Method 3:** Count the points of the Fire and Air divisions across all 16 houses, and count the points of the Water and Earth elements. If the former count is higher, the patient will recover. If the latter count is higher, they will not recover.

**Method 4:** If the figures <term>☰ ⚇ ☰ ⚇</term> are predominant in the <term>Kundali</term><note>The geomantic chart or horoscope</note>, know that the patient's end is near. Specifically, this figure <term>☰</term> is a definite <term>Marak</term><note>Death-inflicting sign</note> at the time of a query regarding a patient.

If inauspicious figures are in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses <note>The 'Kendra' or angular houses</note>, the ship will sink. If both auspicious and inauspicious figures are present, it will sink but then stay afloat <note>Likely meaning it will be salvaged or survive the wreck</note>. If 🝟 🝠 🝙 are in the 1st house with a complaint in a strong house, and inauspicious figures are in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th, it will sink or get stuck. If 🝙 🝚 🝛 are in the 1st and there is a complaint in the 7th, 11th, or 13th, it will reach its destination safely and return.

**In what condition is the traveler? —** Count the points of the <term>indicators</term><note>The dots forming the geomantic figures</note> from the 1st house to the 14th house. If those points total 32, he is in trouble but will ultimately find happiness. If there is an auspicious figure in the 1st house, it is good. If there is an inauspicious or mediocre figure, he is unhappy.

**When and in what state will the traveler arrive? —** Count all the indicator points in the <term>horoscope</term><note>original: "kundali"; the geomantic chart</note> and divide that total by 4. If the remainder is 1, he will come quickly; if 2, with delay; if 3, he will go further and then return; if 4 <note>zero remainder</note>, his arrival is doubtful.

**Method 2: —** By the <term>multiplication</term><note>The process of combining two geomantic figures to produce a third</note> of the figures in the 1st and 9th houses, if the resulting figure is 🝒, he will come late. If 🝓, he will come quickly. If 🝡, he will come in sorrow. If 🝠, he will come with unattainable gains. If 🝙, he will come with wealth and grain. If 🝚, he will come sick. If 🝛, he will come quickly with grief and anxiety. If 🝜, he will come with delay. If 🝝, he will come unhappy due to bile-related ailments <note>referring to the Ayurvedic 'Pitta' humor</note>. If 🝞, he is on the way. If 🝟, he will come poor and with enmity. If 🝖, he is in trouble on the way. If 🝔, he is absorbed in worldly affairs and will come late. If 🝒, he is on the way.

**Method 3: —** If there is an auspicious figure in the 5th house and a complaint in an auspicious house, he is at ease. If there is a complaint of inauspicious figures in inauspicious houses, he is unhappy.

*   **1st House figure:** Indicates if it is soft or hard.
*   **2nd House:** Indicates the color.
*   **3rd House:** Indicates the shape and beauty.
*   **4th House:** Indicates weight, smell, and value.
*   **5th House:** Indicates qualities/properties.
*   **6th House:** Indicates the origin.
*   **7th House:** Indicates things related to that substance.
*   **8th House:** Indicates if it is a single item or many.
*   **9th House:** Indicates the taste.
*   **10th House:** Indicates if it is whole or half.
*   **11th House:** Indicates the place of origin.
*   **12th House:** Indicates if it is of mineral origin.

If it belongs to the **Earth element**, it is unrecognizable and black.

### Predicting Questions from the 10th House.

> <note>original: "राज्याधिकारयो:कीर्ते: श्रेष्ठत्वस्यनृपस्य च ॥ बलतंत्रोद्यमस्यापि चौषधस्यगुरोरपि ॥ ४३ ॥ जनन्याश्चापिसेवाया मेघानांभ्र यंत्रयो: ॥ स्वज्ञाते:स्वामिनश्चापि वैद्यानांदशमाद्वदेत् ॥ ४४ ॥"</note>
> From the tenth house, one should predict matters regarding sovereign power, authority, fame, excellence, the king, military strength, administration, effort, medicine, the teacher (Guru), the mother, service, clouds, travel, one's own kin, the master, and physicians.

**In what condition will this kingdom function?**— If the <term>Shakals</term><note>Geomantic figures or symbols formed by dots and lines</note> in houses 1 and 10 are $\begin{smallmatrix} \circ \\ \circ \\ \circ \\ \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Via</note>, $\begin{smallmatrix} - \\ - \\ - \\ - \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Populus</note>, or $\begin{smallmatrix} \circ \\ \circ \\ \circ \\ \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Via</note>, the kingdom will last for many days and will be governed by strict authority. With the $\begin{smallmatrix} - \\ - \\ - \\ - \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Populus</note> figure, the kingdom will either deteriorate while functioning or meet a bad end. With $\begin{smallmatrix} - \\ - \\ \circ \\ \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Acquisitio</note>, even if there is significant profiteering and betrayal within the state, the administration will proceed peacefully. With $\begin{smallmatrix} - \\ - \\ \circ \\ \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Acquisitio</note>, it will initially proceed peacefully but eventually, a bad administration will begin. With $\begin{smallmatrix} \circ \\ \circ \\ \circ \\ \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Via</note>, the state of the kingdom will not go well. ### Are the witnesses truthful? — 
If the figure resulting from the multiplication of the figures in houses 1, 4, 7, and 10 is then multiplied by the figure in the 15th house, and the resulting figure is <term>Laetitia</term> <note>original: [- - - ⁚]</note>, <term>Acquisitio</term> <note>original: [⁚ - - -]</note>, or <term>Populus</term> <note>original: [- - - -]</note>, then the witnesses are truthful. If the result is <term>Albus</term> <note>original: [⁚ - ⁚ -]</note>, <term>Conjunctio</term> <note>original: [- ⁚ - ⁚]</note>, <term>Puella</term> <note>original: [- - ⁚ ⁚]</note>, or <term>Puer</term> <note>original: [⁚ ⁚ - -]</note>, then some are truthful and some are false. If the result is <term>Acquisitio</term> <note>original: [⁚ - - -]</note>, <term>Laetitia</term> <note>original: [- - - ⁚]</note>, <term>Via</term> <note>original: [⁚ ⁚ ⁚ ⁚]</note>, or <term>Carcer</term> <note>original: [- ⁚ ⁚ -]</note>, then all are entirely false.

### Have I eaten? — 
If auspicious <term>Entering</term> <note>Dakhil: figures that signify coming in or stability</note> figures are in houses 2 and 6, then the meal has been eaten; if they are <term>Exiting</term> <note>Kharij: figures signifying departure or loss</note>, then no. If there is an <term>Entering</term> figure in the 2nd house and an <term>Exiting</term> figure in the 6th, a small amount has been eaten but the desire to eat remains. If the opposite occurs, no food has been eaten at all. If an inauspicious <term>Munkaloub</term> <note>term: a "reversed" or "turning" figure</note> is in the 6th house, and an auspicious <term>Entering</term> or <term>Munkaloub</term> is in the 2nd, food was eaten but then vomited. If the figures there are auspicious, it was good food; if inauspicious, it was poor quality food. If all figures are <term>Vriddha</term> <note>term: "old" or "aged" figures</note>, one should say the food was stale.

**Method 2:** If the figure in the 10th house is <term>Puer</term> and it sits in an inimical house, the meal has not been eaten. If there are other figures besides this, the meal has not been eaten.

### What have I eaten? — 
If a Fire-element figure is in the 10th house and there is a <term>Takrar</term> <note>term: repetition or "re-occurrence" of a figure in another house</note> in the Fire-element positions, sweet items have been consumed. The 1st house represents the <term>querent</term> <note>original: "प्रश्नकर्त्याचे" - the person asking the question</note> and the 12th house represents the enemy. If there are inauspicious figures in the 1st and 12th houses but they "complain" <note>original: "तक्रार" - a technical term in Ramal where a figure repeats in another house, indicating a connection or 'complaint' between them</note> in the <term>Umhat</term> <note>original: "उमहाता" - likely referring to the 'Mothers' or the primary four figures of the chart</note>, then the enemy will not act on their hostility. If [⁚••⁚] is in the 1st house and "complains" in the 10th, then the querent's officers are not good. If an inauspicious figure is in the 15th house, a bad outcome will result from the querent's own brother. 

If [⁚⁚••] is in the 1st house with a "complaint" in the 15th, and there is no inauspicious figure in the 13th, but "complaints" exist in the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the querent's right hand will be broken. If "complaints" appear in the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, the ears, nose, or fingers will be cut off. If figures such as [•⁚•⁚] [⁚••⁚] [••⁚⁚] [⁚⁚⁚⁚] [••••] are in the 1st house, with "complaints" in the 8th and 12th houses and an inauspicious figure in the 15th, the enemy will shed blood with the intent to kill the querent. If any inauspicious figure is in the 1st house and there is a "complaint" in the 12th, the enemy will keep the querent in captivity, or otherwise commit murder. If [⁚••⁚] [•⁚•⁚] appear in those same houses, the enemy will strike with a whip. If [⁚•⁚•] is present, they will burn or brand the querent. If [•⁚⁚⁚] [⁚⁚•⁚] [••⁚⁚] [⁚⁚⁚⁚] are present, the enemy will hang the querent or otherwise kill them by drowning in water.

If the figure <term>⁑/⁑/⁑/⁑</term> <note>Populus or 'The People'</note> appears in the 1st house and is repeated in the 12th house, and if inauspicious figures appear in the 2nd through 5th houses, the person will be kept in prison.

**What if a loan is given to this person?** — If a favorable figure appears in the 12th house, the loan should be given. The person will become free of debt. If an inauspicious figure appears, they will not be able to repay the debt; therefore, do not give it.

**Will one be liberated from spirit possession?** — If the figure in the 12th house is among <term>⁕/⁕/⁑/⁕</term> <note>Laetitia</note> or <term>⁕/⁑/⁕/⁕</term> <note>Albus</note>, one will soon be liberated through the service of deities and the Guru. If the Water element points are greater, there will be heavy rain. And if the Earth element points are greater, there will be a famine.

Due to the absence [of rain], crops will wither and a famine will occur. $\begin{smallmatrix} \circ \\ \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>The figure 'Populus' or People</note> Rain will be scarce; though signs of clouds will eventually appear, there will be a slight period of plenty. $\begin{smallmatrix} \circ & \circ \\ & \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>The figure 'Laetitia' or Joy</note> Rain will be excessive and the harvest will be good. $\begin{smallmatrix} & \circ \\ \circ & \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>The figure 'Albus' or White</note> Rain and wind will increase. $\begin{smallmatrix} \circ & \circ \\ \circ & \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>The figure 'Acquisitio' or Gain</note> Rain will be abundant and the harvest will be excellent.

**How is the day today?** — If the figures in positions 14, 15, and 16 are <term>Dakhol</term> <note>Entering/Inward-moving figures</note> and are auspicious, it is excellent and profit will be gained. Success will be achieved if any work is commenced. If they are inauspicious, it is bad. If the figures are <term>Kharij</term> <note>Exiting/Outward-moving</note> or <term>Munkaloj</term> <note>Mobile/Changing</note> and inauspicious, there is neither profit nor loss. If those figures are auspicious, even if profit occurs, it will be spent. If they are <term>Sabit</term> <note>Stable/Fixed</note> figures, expenses will occur after a delay.

**Method 2:** — In the <term>Kundali</term> <note>The geomantic chart or square</note>, positions 1-2-3-4-9-10-13-15 belong to the twelve hours of the day, and positions 5-6-7-8-11-12-14-16 belong to the twelve hours of the night. These 8 positions should be divided at a rate of 1.5 hours per position. Similarly, the 8 night positions should be assigned 1.5 hours each. By considering the <term>Tatva-vibhag</term> <note>Elemental division</note> of the figure in each position, one should determine whether each specific time is good or bad. Furthermore, the elements of Fire, Air, Water, and Earth are present in every figure; one should give the prediction by taking the "manifest element" as an example. 

**Example** — The 1st position in the chart represents 1.5 hours from sunrise. If the figure $\equiv$ <note>The figure 'Via' or Way</note> falls in that position, then because all four elements are "hidden" in it, that 1.5-hour period is of no use for any work of the querent; on the contrary, it will cause loss. Now, suppose the figure $\begin{smallmatrix} \circ & \circ \\ \circ & \circ \end{smallmatrix}$ <note>Acquisitio</note> falls in that place; this figure is auspicious and is "manifest" through the three elements of Fire, Air, and Earth. The prediction should be given based on the qualities of Fire, Air, Earth, etc., using the previously mentioned tables and supporting materials.

<meta>This page continues the technical explanation of the Ramala (geomancy) system, specifically focusing on the mathematical calculation of outcomes based on specific question codes (Chahavanka).</meta>

<page-num>113</page-num>

Multiply the first <term>Shakal</term><note>A geomantic figure or sign composed of four lines of dots or dashes.</note> by the first figure. Then, determine the numerical value of the resulting figure according to the *A-Ba-Ja-Da* sequence <note>A traditional alphanumeric system used in geomancy to assign values to the four levels of a figure.</note> and set that number aside. Next, determine the numerical value of the figure corresponding to the third fixed point using the same *A-Ba-Ja-Da* sequence. Add both numbers together and count from the "Intention House" <note>The specific house in the chart representing the querent's desire.</note> (starting from 1-2) until the total is reached. Based on the auspicious or inauspicious qualities of the figure where the count ends, the outcome of the task should be predicted.

**Example:** A gentleman asks the question, "Will I meet my friend?" In the *Chahavank* table, this question is the 4th in the group of questions for the 1st House. Next to the sentence "Meeting a friend," the code numbers 5-9-14 are written. The first digit is 5.

Counting from the 1st Intention House, the figure in the 5th position is <term>|°°°</term>. By multiplying the figure <term>°|°°</term> from the 1st Intention House by this figure, the figure <term>°||°</term> is produced. The second code number is 9. In the 9th position from the Intention House is the figure <term>|°°|</term>. By multiplying the previous figure <term>°||°</term> by this figure <term>|°°|</term>, the figure <term>°||°</term> is formed. Its value according to the *A-Ba-Ja-Da* sequence is 3 (refer to Part 1 regarding counting zeros and excluding lines, etc.). Now, the third code number is 14. In the 14th position from the 1st Intention House is the figure <term>°||°</term>; its *A-Ba-Ja-Da* value is 7. Adding the previous 3 and this 7 results in the number 10. Now, as per the method described, counting from the 1st Intention House, the count ends at the 10th position. At that position is the figure <term>°||°</term>. Since this is <term>Shubha Kharij</term><note>original: "शुभ खारीज" - An auspicious figure indicating outward movement or successful departure.</note>, the meeting will occur with great joy, and there will be conversation regarding trade, industry, state affairs, the mother's well-being, etc. Because it is a *Kharij* (outward) figure, one will have to return soon. In this manner, astrologers should gather all necessary tools and materials and answer the group of questions using these *Chahavank* codes.

# Part 3.

## Analysis of Results for Years, Months, Days, etc.

->[Decorative floral ornament]<-

The astrologer <note>original: "Jyotishi"</note> should rise early in the morning when the Sun enters the tropical sign of Aries <note>The vernal equinox, marking the beginning of the solar year</note>. After completing their religious duties such as bathing and morning prayers <note>original: "Sandhyadi karma"</note> according to the law, they should joyfully remember their chosen deity and their Guru. After reciting the mantra mentioned in Part 1 seven times, they should construct a horoscope <note>original: "Kundali"</note> before noon—either for the entire world, for a specific country, or to address the joys and sorrows of a specific petitioner—and then analyze the results for that year.

**Analysis of the Year's Results:** If a favorable figure <note>original: "Shakal"; refers to the geomantic signs</note> is in the 1st house of the horoscope, there will be great physical happiness. If the figure is malefic <note>original: "Papi"</note> and weak, the body will suffer extreme hardship. If that figure is malefic but strong, there will be moderate happiness. The results for all 12 houses should be analyzed in this same manner. Now, following the sequence of omens, if a figure is in its own house, even if it is malefic, the results related to that house will increase. And if that figure in its own house is fully strong, the benefits of that house will be even greater.

**Method 2:** If an "Outgoing" <note>original: "Kharij"; a geomantic term for figures moving outward</note> figure is in the 1st house, there will be no growth in the matters related to that house. If it is an "Incoming" <note>original: "Dakhil"</note> figure, there will be growth. If that "Incoming" figure is fully strong, the results of that house will be abundant. If it is a "Mutable" <note>original: "Munkalib"</note> figure, the results of that house will decrease; if it is "Fixed" <note>original: "Sabit"</note>, the results of that house will increase. If a "Fixed" figure is weak, the results will be moderate, and if a "Fixed" figure is fully strong, the results will be superior. Furthermore, if the figures in those houses "testify" <note>original: "Takrar"; a technical term for the repetition or movement of figures between houses</note> in favorable houses, the result is auspicious; if they testify in unfavorable houses, the result is inauspicious; and if they testify in neutral houses, the result should be known as moderate.

**Analysis of the Month's Results:** The figures located from the 1st house to the 12th house of the horoscope represent each month in sequence. The analysis of the monthly results should be done using these figures: the 1st month is analyzed by the figure in the 1st house, the 2nd month by the figure in the 2nd house, and so on for all 12 months...

One should consider: if the <term>figure</term><note>original: "shakal/shakl" refers to the geomantic figures formed by points</note> in the 1st house belongs to a favorable planet and is strong, then the physical comforts and results for that month will be excellent. If it is favorable but weak, the physical comforts will be average. If it is weak and belongs to a malevolent planet, then instead of comfort, there will be suffering for the body during that month. And if that figure <term>makes a complaint</term><note>original: "takrar" refers to the movement or repetition of a figure from one house to another</note> in a favorable house, there will be generally good results that month. If that figure is unfavorable and makes a complaint in a mediocre house, then that month will be average.

If that figure is formed from two favorable figures, the physical comfort in that month will be excellent; if it is produced from unfavorable figures, the results for that month will be undesirable. If produced from mediocre figures, the results will be average. If both [parent figures] are favorable but it is produced from a malevolent figure, physical comfort in that month will be of a mixed nature. If a figure produced from weak and malevolent figures is itself weak, then instead of happiness, various types of calamities will arise and wealth etc. will be destroyed during that month.

And if that figure is produced from two figures that are weak and favorable, then all results like physical comfort will proceed moderately during that month. Furthermore, if there is a friendship between the <term>element</term><note>original: "tattva" refers to Earth, Water, Fire, or Air</note> of that figure and the element of the house where it makes a complaint, there will be excellent physical happiness in that month. If there is enmity, there will be more hardship in that month.

If there is friendship between the monthly figure and the figure of the <term>root house</term><note>original: "mula sthana"</note>, the results for physical comfort will be excellent. If the figure resulting from the <term>multiplication</term><note>original: "gunakarane" refers to the geomantic process of combining two figures to form a third</note> of the monthly figure and the figure of the house where the root figure complains is favorable, then all works in that month will be auspicious; if it is unfavorable and weak, many calamities will arise in that month.

If the <term>witness house</term><note>original: "sakshisthana"</note> of that figure is strong, that month will pass happily. And if the figure in the witness house is weak, that month will be undesirable. If the figure of that witness house is formed by the union of two favorable figures, that month will be pleasant. If there is friendship between the element of that figure and the element in the witness house, or if both are the same, the happiness in that month will be excellent, and if there is enmity, there will be hardship. If the witness-figure of that monthly figure makes a complaint in a house belonging to a favorable figure, there will be more auspiciousness in that month. And if it is unfavorable, there will be more hardship. The element of the house where that monthly figure makes a complaint and its...

If there is a friendship between the principle of the Witness Position <note>original: "Sakshisthan"; the 15th house in a geomantic chart used for verification</note> and the current month's ruler, then the results for that month, such as physical comforts and health, will be excellent. However, if there is enmity between them, various types of sorrows will arise. When considering a specific monthly figure <note>original: "shakal"; the four-line binary symbols used in geomancy</note>, one should look at the second figure belonging to its ruler; if both are auspicious, the month will be highly favorable. If they are inauspicious, the results will be undesirable. If they are of average strength <term>Bali</term><note>refers to the "strength" or "potency" of a symbol in a specific house</note>, the results for that month will be mediocre. This is the method for one month. In this same manner, one should consider all 12 months and the results of the wealth-cycle <note>original: "anudhan chakra"</note> before giving an answer; by doing so, the prediction will not fail.

### Proven Charts for Understanding Periodical Results

After casting the dice and creating the initial chart, take the figures from the 13th, 10th, 11th, and 14th positions directly to prepare a second chart. In that newly prepared chart, if the figure in the 1st house is identical to the 13th, the 2nd identical to the 10th, the 3rd identical to the 11th, and the 4th identical to the 14th, then that chart is called "Proven" <term>Sabit</term><note>from the Arabic/Persian 'thabit' meaning fixed or proven; a state of mathematical equilibrium in the chart</note>. If the chart does not become "Proven" in this way, take the figures from the 13th, 10th, 11th, and 14th positions of that second chart and prepare a third chart as before. If it is still not proven, repeat the process. This calculation can go up to six charts. Including the initial query chart, it must become "Proven" within six charts. For example, see the query chart below. To achieve proof from it, four subsequent charts were made. That is, it became "Proven" in the fifth chart.

-> Results of the Stable Chart <-

If the stability <note>the matching of figures</note> occurs in the 1st chart, there will be gain of wealth and the body will experience happiness in every way.
If it occurs in the 2nd, there will be extreme happiness in all respects.
If it occurs in the 3rd, there will be immense acquisition of wealth that year.
If it occurs in the 4th, all results for that year will be mediocre.
If it occurs in the 5th, the body will suffer great hardship during that year.
If it occurs in the 6th, there will be death or death-like suffering in that year.

**Method for calculating Chart-Period, Month-Period, and Subtle-Period and their results:** Take the number of the chart in which the stability occurs. Divide 365 days, 15 <term>Ghatika</term> <note>a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note>, and 31 <term>Pala</term> <note>a unit of time equal to 24 seconds</note> by that number. The resulting quotient is the <term>Kundali-Dasha</term> <note>Chart-Period</note>. Divide that Chart-Period by 12; the resulting quotient is the <term>Sukshma-Dasha</term> <note>Subtle-Period</note>.

When the number is divided by 365 days, 15 ghatikas <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note>, and 31 palas <note>A unit of time equal to 24 seconds</note>, the result is 73 days, 3 ghatikas,
<gloss>5</gloss>
and 65 palas; this represents the duration of the <term>Kundali Dasha</term> <note>A major planetary period in a horoscope</note>. By dividing these 73 days, 3 ghatikas, and 65 palas
<gloss>12</gloss>
by 12, the result is 6 days, 15 ghatikas, and 31 palas, which belongs to the <term>Sukshma Dasha</term> <note>A subtle or minor sub-period used for precise timing</note>. One should determine the <term>Shakal</term> <note>The geomantic figure or sign formed in Ramal astrology</note> of the Sukshma Dasha by multiplying the Shakal of the Kundali Dasha by the Shakal of the Sukshma Dasha.

If the resulting Shakal is auspicious and is positioned in an auspicious house as a <term>Takrar</term> <note>original: "तक्रार" - in Ramal, this refers to the repetition or "argument" of a figure in another house</note> and is strong, the body will experience excellent comforts, financial gain, destruction of enemies, and meetings with friends, among other excellent results. If it is inauspicious but makes a Takrar in an auspicious house, the results will be mediocre. If it is inauspicious, positioned in an inauspicious house as a Takrar, and is weak, it should be known as unfavorable.

The results of the Shakals placed in the sixteen houses— 7: If this falls in the 1st house, one will meet honorable gentlemen and gain superior objects. In the 2nd, there will be profit in buying and selling, excellent thoughts, and one's own money will be spent. In the 3rd, there will be a short journey for the sake of brothers and sisters. In the 4th, there will be thoughts regarding one's own house and gains in earnings, joy from the father, and help from friends. In the 5th, news of children or friends will be heard, and illness will be cured. In the 6th, there will be loss caused by servants, servants and animals will remain in bondage, illness will be cured, and a secret matter will be revealed. In the 7th, marriage and the <term>birth of a son</term> <note>original: "पुत्रोत्पत्ती"</note>. In the 8th, one's own legal claim will proceed in the government. In the 9th, there will be gain of good objects, a long-distance journey, and one will have good dreams. In the 10th, there will be great honor from a King, an official, or a wealthy person. A woman will give a blessing that brings joy to the mind. In the 11th, the patronage of scholars, happiness, and joy. In the 12th, the destruction of <term>four-legged animals</term> <note>original: "चतुष्पाद" - usually referring to livestock or cattle</note> and loss caused by enemies. In the 13th, travel and profit through the patronage of the wealthy. In the 14th, protection/assurance from a great gentleman. In the 16th, the destruction of all works.

## Yearly Predictions for the Country

As previously described, prepare the *Sabit Kundali* <note>A "Proven Chart" or fixed geomantic square used in Ramal astrology</note>. In whichever chart the proof is established, take the figures from houses 1 $\times$ 13, 4 $\times$ 14, 7 $\times$ 15, and 10 $\times$ 16. Multiply the figures in these positions by each other to create 4 new figures. Then, multiply those four figures sequentially with each other to produce one final figure (*Shakal*). If that final figure is auspicious and strong, the country will experience excellent happiness.

**Example:** From the previous *Sabit Kundali*, multiply the figures in positions 1 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ} \times$ 13 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$; 4 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ} \times$ 14 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$; 7 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ} \times$ 15 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$; and 10 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ} \times$ 16 $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$. By sequentially multiplying these figures, these four $\equiv \times \equiv$ and $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ} \times \stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$ figures are formed. After multiplying these four together, these two $\equiv + \stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$ are formed. By multiplying these two again, this final $\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$ figure is produced. The predictions based on this are as follows:

$\stackrel{\circ\circ}{\circ\circ}$ <note>The figure *Jama'at* (The Congregation)</note>: If this figure appears, there will be physical well-being for the people of the country. Everyone will be inclined toward auspicious deeds. Agriculture will flourish, leading to an increase in food supplies. However, in the Northeast corner, there will be either excessive rain or a total drought. There will be loss and fear due to rats, insects, parrots, or the King's military camps being pitched near fields. Fear will also arise from servants or animals like oxen.

$\stackrel{\circ\circ}{—}$ <note>The figure *Farah* (Joy/Success)</note>: Great profit in trade and a focus on the path of merit. Trees will bear many sweet, nectar-like fruits, which the people will enjoy to their heart's content. There will be an increase in the finest goods within the country or the world. The King will find happiness and be devoted to moral conduct and diligent in protecting his subjects (*Prajapalani*). Worldly happiness will be abundant, and life will be fearless without any kind of disturbances. These results will manifest in the Eastern parts of the country or the world.

$\stackrel{—}{\circ\circ}$ <note>The figure *Uqla* (The Bond/Constraint)</note>: People's hearts will be agitated. Rain will not fall, and the heat during the Summer season (*Grishma Ritu*) will be intense. The King will be less unjust <note>original: "अन्याय कमी" - implying a reduction in tyranny or perhaps a specific legal context</note>, but there will be internal quarrels in every household. There will be war in the kingdom, and the influence of the wicked and thieves will prevail. Destruction of property will occur through water and fire. There will be loss of wealth, an increase in poisonous creatures like snakes, scorpions, and dogs, and sudden deaths. These results must be endured by the people in the Southwest regions.

$\equiv$ <note>The figure *Tariq* (The Path)</note>: An increase in goods and materials. All people will conduct themselves ethically and find happiness. There is a slight fear of phlegmatic disorders (*Shleshma Vikar*). This result will occur for those residing in the Western direction.
